title: Python Policy PPF Implementation Policy Sidecar Extension
description: External companion schema for generated Pydantic projections, attrs runtime objects, cattrs adapters, advisory design patterns, and qualified refactoring transformations. The official Python Policy PPF schema remains unchanged and authoritative.
$comment: Register the official schema under urn:python-policy-ppf:generation-policy:0.2.0. This extension is bound to sha256:06055b436bb224a4fc76eef96821d7e467eeb1c047b78807945c22e06d7d4eaf.

x-ppf-invariants.statement: Every shaping predicate references a declared input fact type and is evaluated over an admitted value of that type.
Every decision has true and false targets, every referenced target exists, unreachable nodes are rejected, and cycles are rejected unless explicitly permitted.
Every terminal path selects at least one primary semantic profile; multiple primary profiles are rejected unless the terminal explicitly permits them.
Selected profiles and facets are closed transitively over their requiredProfileRefs before an implementation binding is selected.
A resolved profile and facet set containing a declared conflict is rejected.
Decision records bind immutable subject, policy, registry, and implementation binding content references.
Generated artifacts bind generator identity, generation plan, source inputs, profile selection, annotation policy, and artifact digest.
Optimized implementation bindings pass differential conformance against a qualified reference binding.
Capability providers are declared, validated, and frozen before wiring-plan compilation or runtime resolution.
Dependency validation and runtime resolution consume the same immutable, digest-bound wiring plan.
A longer-lived capability does not retain a dependency from a shorter-lived scope.
Alias validation and lifetime qualification follow transparent bindings to their terminal providers.
Union dependencies require explicit selection and optional dependencies require declared absence semantics.
Container injection is limited to declared composition roots, framework adapters, child-scope builders, and generic integration boundaries.
Managed capabilities bind acquisition and release behavior to a scope and finalize in reverse acquisition order.
Provider registries, wiring plans, compiled resolver graphs, overlays, and runtime assembly records are bound by immutable content digests.
A test-harness adapter exposes a selected capability root as one external graph node without reproducing the internal provider graph.
A projected fixture does not outlive its container fixture or the resolved capability scope.
Bulk fixture names are checked for collisions before an explicitly selected target module is modified.
